label: MUSIC 2.0
note: Fresh sci-fi scores. Not conditioned on the live beds. Not Codex's audition rounds.

tracks.title: Night Run
tracks.note: Nocturnal analog score: electric piano, lonely lead, rain on a city that does not know it is being saved. Slow, aching, human-scale science fiction.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre

tracks.title: The Ring
tracks.note: Analog score for the night the relay ring wakes. A rising lead over electric piano, then the phrase answered from far away.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre
the rising phrase answered from farther away

tracks.title: Hold
tracks.note: A clock in a cathedral: pipe-organ ostinato, ticking, strings that refuse to let go. Relentless, guttural, then the sky opens.

tracks.title: Latency
tracks.note: A melody stated in a coastal hangar, then answered 2.6 seconds later — thinner, farther, the same phrase arriving from the Moon.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre
a second thinner analog voice answering the melody late
the late answering voice still present

tracks.title: Richmond Street
tracks.note: A falling analog theme over a city afternoon. Slow, human, irreversible.

positive_styles: analog brass in a minor hymn
electric piano alone with the theme

tracks.title: Eleven Seconds
tracks.note: A four-note analog elegy. Electric piano, lonely lead, C-sharp minor. The melody keeps going.

positive_styles: a four-note melody stated on the first beat
lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre

tracks.title: The First Walk
tracks.note: Analog wonder looking up. A rising three-note motif, Earthlight, a hand against the sky.

positive_styles: analog brass opening toward C major

tracks.title: The Clone
tracks.note: Year two: the garage is an office, then a cheaper copy of you takes the sky.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre

tracks.title: Ninety-One Billion
tracks.note: Someone else rings the bell. Cold analog triumph that does not belong to you.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre
a bright analog melody that feels expensive
the melody climbing, still not yours

tracks.title: Eighteen Months
tracks.note: A worn analog campaign. The same melody, older, still going.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre
the same theme, thinner and stubborn
electric piano left holding the line

tracks.title: The People's Network
tracks.note: Your IPO. Warm analog hymn. A woman in house slippers rings the city open.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre
the melody opening, human and earned

tracks.title: Year Three
tracks.note: An ordinary Monday that is also a company. Analog, precise, heavier than it looks.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre

tracks.title: The Shoebox
tracks.note: A home elegy. Analog piano and a small melody that will not get bigger.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre

tracks.title: The Honest Delay
tracks.note: Your second bell. Analog, precise, the honest share price as a melody.

positive_styles: lonely analog lead with saxophone timbre
a clear analog melody, no swagger

tracks.title: First Rung
tracks.note: Interstellar family. Organ as a construction engine. Ticking, 12/8, C-sharp minor. A platform is a machine that learned to house people.

positive_styles: pipe organ treated as a construction engine

tracks.title: Aurelia
tracks.note: Interstellar family. Organ ostinato as a country founding. D minor, 12/8, 88 BPM. Vast and unresolved — not a civic hymn.

positive_styles: pipe organ ostinato as a country founding

tracks.title: The Road Open
tracks.note: Interstellar family. Organ as a spacecraft engine. 5/4 docking ostinato, F minor. A schoolteacher rides a machine into the sky.

positive_styles: pipe organ treated as a spacecraft engine
